Naproxen was discontinued with dramatic improvement of jaundice and return of liver-function tests to normal after four weeks. The authors state that the acuteness of onset with hepatocellular injury and cholestasis in this patient after naproxen suggested a drug-induced hepatitis.
raw.extra_details: Dose 250 mg twice daily; jaundice and abdominal pain began about one week after starting naproxen. Hepatitis-associated antigen negative. Liver scan confirmed enlarged liver with no metastases; bone scan normal. Dechallenge led to dramatic improvement with liver-function tests returning to normal after four weeks. Patient had prior mastectomy (1957) and rheumatoid arthritis since 1964. A prior report described jaundice of a cholestatic nature with naproxen therapy.

Day +30 mortality (P=0.36), nonrelapse mortality (P=0.42) and overall survival (P=0.55) were not statistically significantly different between patients with grade III/IV vs grade 0–II liver toxicity. Adverse events per CTCAE v4.0 after CLARA I: hepatobiliary disorders grade 3 52%/grade 4 1%; AST/ALT increased grade 3 44%; bilirubin increased grade 3 10%. The case was reported to the regional pharmacovigilance center. Nimesulide has been suspected of increased hepatotoxicity since market launch: it was withdrawn in Finland and Spain in 2002 after an incidence of hepatic events reported ~100-fold higher than other NSAIDs, the Irish Medicines Board suspended it in May 2007 after 53 hepatic adverse-effect reports since 1995 including 3 deaths from acute liver failure, and EMEA added warnings with a 15-day treatment limit. The hepatic injury is described as idiosyncratic, unpredictable and dose-independent, with a typical latency of 3-15 weeks (8 weeks in this case), most often presenting as cholestatic jaundice with hepatic cytolysis that regresses on drug withdrawal, with rare fatal cases.
raw.extra_details: Index case: latency ~8 weeks; TP 12%, factor V 13%, stage III encephalopathy, Glasgow 6; transjugular biopsy showed edematous necrotic parenchyma with eosinophilic and lymphocytic infiltrates; explant showed extensive necrosis with lymphocytic, plasmocytic, eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltrates; patient listed in super-urgency for liver transplant, placed on MARS, transplanted, survived; case reported to regional pharmacovigilance center. Regulatory/history: Finland withdrew 2002 (incidence ~100x other NSAIDs); Spain withdrew 2002; EMEA 2005 risk/benefit favored benefit with labeling warnings, contraindication in hepatic insufficiency and transaminase monitoring; Irish Medicines Board suspended May 2007 after 53 hepatic adverse-effect reports since 1995 including 3 deaths from acute liver failure; EMEA then proposed 15-day treatment limit and contraindication in alcoholics and in combination with other hepatotoxic drugs; never approved in USA, Canada, Australia, UK, or New Zealand. China... Mechanism: idiosyncratic reaction attributed to abnormal metabolites in genetically susceptible individuals, either directly toxic or recognized as antigen by host immune system. Phenotype: typically cholestatic jaundice with cytolysis regressing on drug stop; latency 3-15 weeks; rare fatal cases; one prior published fulminant hepatitis case in France requiring transplant.

raw.support_text: This case report describes, to the authors' knowledge, the first report of everolimus-associated DILI. In a post-transplant patient, everolimus was introduced (replacing mycophenolic acid) during a renal-sparing study while tacrolimus was continued. Liver enzymes rose to peak values (ALT 149 IU/L, AST 81 IU/L, ALP 215 IU/L) roughly two and a half months after starting everolimus; a liver biopsy showed mild patchy sinusoidal dilatation with focal mild inflammatory infiltrate containing lymphocytes, eosinophils, and rare acidophil bodies, considered consistent with the possibility of drug injury, with no evidence of acute rejection. After everolimus discontinuation, liver enzymes returned to normal within one week. Everolimus was ranked as having 'ambiguous DILI concern' in a human reference drug list, since no verified causality evidence reports on DILI existed.
raw.qualifying_conditions: Post-transplant (renal transplant) patient on a clinical research renal-sparing protocol; everolimus co-administered with tacrolimus (continued throughout), replacing mycophenolic acid; unresolved co-exposure setting.
raw.extra_details: Biopsy findings included mild portal inflammation with lymphocytes, pericentral sinusoidal dilatation, and inflammation adjacent to the central vein (first biopsy, RAI 1/9), and mild patchy sinusoidal dilatation with lymphocytes, eosinophils, and rare acidophil bodies (second biopsy, 11/30/15); no acute cellular rejection (RAI 1/9); no duct injury, duct loss, cholestasis, endothelitis, or steatosis; no fever, rash, or acute hypersensitivity reaction; HBsAg/HBcAg immunostains negative. Everolimus dose up to 3 mg qam/2.5 mg qpm (max 5.5 mg daily), trough reached 3.8 ng/mL; tacrolimus troughs 6.9-9.8 ng/mL. Peak enzymes ALT 149, AST 81, ALP 215 IU/L; total bilirubin 0.23 mg/dL. Enzymes normalized one week after discontinuation (ALT 22, AST 20, ALP 105). Everolimus has high lipophilicity (logP 5.01) and a stable 2-hydroxy-ethyl substitution at position 40; daily dose far below the 100 mg DILI-model threshold. Ranked 'ambiguous DILI concern' in a human DILI reference list; initially 'less DILI concern' based on trial data (<=10% with ALP/transaminase elevations).

Nefazodone prescribed to 10.5 million patients worldwide with approximately 22 reported cases (approximate rate of 1 per 250,000-300,000). No fatal or transplant severity reported; DILI relationship is a trial-derived association, not causal attribution.
raw.extra_details: Abiraterone acetate (COU-AA-301): hepatotoxicity 15% all grades, 4% grade ≥3; COU-AA-302: 25% all grades, 8% grade ≥3. Pooled CYP-17 inhibitor analysis for hepatotoxicity: all-grade RR 1.93 (1.15-3.24), p=0.01, I²=85%; grade 3-4 RR 2.94 (0.95-9.08), p=0.06, I²=86%. Hepatotoxicity tabulated as 'abnormalities in liver function tests'; where ALT and AST increases were reported separately, incidence was summed.
